The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
return Collections.unmodifiableCollection(
        getCredentialsInternal().getAllTokens());
```
Reason:
This line returns an unmodifiable view of the collection obtained from `getCredentialsInternal().getAllTokens()`. If this collection is modified while being iterated over, it results in a `ConcurrentModificationException`, as the internal state of the credentials is directly linked to the returned collection.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
return new ArrayList<Token<?>>(getCredentialsInternal().getAllTokens());
```
Reason:
This line creates a new `ArrayList` containing the tokens from `getCredentialsInternal().getAllTokens()`, ensuring that the returned collection is a separate copy. This prevents any concurrent modifications to the original collection from affecting the returned list, thus avoiding the `ConcurrentModificationException`.
